Breadcrumb

Where the current page sits in the app, as a line of links to each page above it.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • On a page two or more levels below a destination, such as a run inside a repository, so the reader can go up to any level.
  • At the regular width, above the page header. On a phone it may stand in the same place, or the back link in the app header may do the job alone.

When not to use it

  • On a top-level destination. There is nothing above it to link to.
  • For the steps of a task in progress. Those are steps, not places, so write them in the page.
  • For going back one level only. Use the back link in the app header.
  • For moving between sibling screens. Use the sidebar nav or the tab bar.

Sizes

default
One line, 44px tall. Below 768px each item between the first and the last is at most 88px wide and is cut with an ellipsis. At 768px and up they show in full and shrink only when the line is full.

Accessibility

  • Use a nav element with aria-label="Breadcrumb" holding an ol with the ds-breadcrumb__list class. Each li has the ds-breadcrumb__item class, in order from the top level down.
  • Every page above the current one is a link with the ds-breadcrumb__link class. The current page is the last item, a span with the ds-breadcrumb__current class and aria-current="page". It is text, never a link.
  • The chevrons between items are drawn by the stylesheet and are not read out. Type no separator into the markup.
  • A link is underlined at rest and the current page is heavier, so the two never differ by colour alone.
  • An item that is cut still has its full text in the markup, so a screen reader reads all of it. The page it links to shows the full name as its title.
  • Tab moves through the links in order and Enter follows one. Both come from the link element. The current page is not a tab stop.
  • The component needs no script.

Classes

  • ds-breadcrumb
  • ds-breadcrumb__current
  • ds-breadcrumb__item
  • ds-breadcrumb__link
